claims.text: The AWSx ELB component integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC to give compute running in AWS configurable network accessibility.
The example load balancer listens on port 80 in the account's per-region default VPC using its public subnets, exposing it to the internet.
The Pulumi AWS registry has API docs for the LaunchTemplate resource at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/.
AWSx uses the load balancer target group passed in an ECS task definition's portMappings to populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration.
The AWSx ECS component (awsx.ecs classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules for load balancer targets.
The awsx-load-balanced-fargate-nginx example program exports a stack output named `url`.
ALBs offer two features that make them more attractive than NLBs for ECS: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
By default, the load balancer is created as internet-facing, using the VPC's public subnets.
The load balancer accepts either a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs) for an explicit list of subnets.
NLB listener protocols support TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC, while ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP.
AWS docs on fixed-response and redirect actions are at rule-action-types.html anchors #fixed-response-actions and #redirect-actions.
AWS documentation about listener rules is at elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/listener-rules.html.
Target group deregistrationDelay range is 0–3600 seconds, default 300.
Target group slowStart range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable; disabled by default.
targetType possible values are instance, ip, lambda, and alb, default instance; IPs must be in VPC private subnet range, RFC 1918, or RFC 6598 (100.64.0.0/10).
Health check interval range is 5–300 seconds, default 30.
healthyThreshold range is 2–10, default 3.
unhealthyThreshold range is 2–10, default 3; for NLBs it must equal healthyThreshold.
Health check timeout range is 2–120 seconds; AWS default is 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
